thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: v6 data path errors observed in us-east-2 (AZ2) -> high packet loss to external customers. Priority: P1. Paging devon (eng-oncall)

devon (eng-oncall): got it, paging neteng and SRE. I'm looking at the egress gateway logs now. can someone post affected ASNs/customers?

noc: Observed from our edge: ICMP "frag needed" and TTL=0 style traces to several downstream prefixes. DNS lookups fine internally but resolution to some endpoints times out from AZ2 only.

sam (neteng): seeing a pattern: IPv6 PMTUD ICMP unreachable/frag messages are not being delivered back to clients. Looks like an MTU mismatch on an upstream transit link combined with DF flags set by our load balancers.

pat (infra): confirming an MTU discrepancy between AZ2 spine (<1500) and the new NIC jumbo config on a subset of hosts (9000). That plus DF on the path will drop large packets.

devon (eng-oncall): can we confirm service impact?

customer-ops: A few customers reporting timeouts for large uploads and websocket disconnects. Beta cohort and one enterprise (AcmeCorp) on dedicated Dedicated pools in us-east-2. Ticket #INC-5421 open.

grace (sre): summary for handoff: traffic from AZ2 egress to certain IPv6 prefixes fails on large packets. Symptoms: slow/failed embeddings, streaming disconnects. Root suspect: PMTUD + jumbo frames + ICMP filtering upstream.

sam (neteng): quick checks: `ip -6 route get` traces show PMTU discovery returns 1500 to some routes, but the DF/DF-like behaviour upstream leads to silent drops. tcpdump from gateway: ```06:12:33.123 IP6 host A > host B: frag needed, mtu 1500``` but no ICMP echo back to our LB VIPs.

devon (eng-oncall): mitigation plan options: 1) clamp MSS on egress GW to 1360 for IPv6 2) rollback jumbo on affected hosts to 1500 3) add route-based failover of customer traffic to AZ4. Which is fastest?

pat (infra): fastest is MSS clamp on egress GW + add short-lived iptables rule for IPv6 MSS clamping. I can push that within 5m.

sam (neteng): also suggest temporary DNS steering: shift affected customer subnets to our us-east-4 endpoints while we mitigate. But that's more involved (certs, config).

devon (eng-oncall): proceed with MSS clamp now. pat, can you apply and confirm with synthetic tests? grace, you'll take lead on customer comms and postmortem ownership. Sam, please validate upstream transit ICMP policy with provider.

pat (infra): applying MSS clamp on egress gateways in AZ2 now: ```ip6tables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -m tcpmss --mss 1361:65535 -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360``` pushing via orchestration. rolling to all gateways in AZ2 (3 nodes)

deploy-bot: Rollout started for infra change: 3 targets in us-east-2 -> 0/3 complete

pat (infra): rollout 1/3 done, testing...

pat (infra): rollout 2/3 done. quick smoke: large upload to AcmeCorp test prefix now succeeds (was failing before).

devon (eng-oncall): synthetic probes show RTT stable and no packet loss for 1400B+ payloads now. Can we confirm stability across all gateways?

pat (infra): rollout 3/3 done. All gateways show MSS clamped. tcpdump now shows fewer ICMP frag needed messages; hosts accepting larger senders/receivers.

sam (neteng): I spoke with transit provider, they confirmed an ACL was dropping some ICMPv6 type 2 messages on a subset of peering links — they will remove filter in 2 hours. Until then MSS clamp + rollback not needed.

grace (sre): customer impact update: ~90% of affected sessions recovered after MSS clamp. Two enterprise customers (AcmeCorp + Beta LLC) saw partial data loss for long-lived connections; we've opened support tickets and started mitigation steps with them (connection retries). Notifying CS to offer credits if SLA hit.

devon (eng-oncall): moving to monitoring phase. keeping alert open until transit provider confirms ICMP fixes and our telemetry stable for 1h. Grace to take the on-call next 8h. I'm handing off. Key notes: MSS clamp applied, backlog of hosts with jumbo config flagged for audit, follow-up action: deploy permanent MSS clamp in network policy, run infra change to normalize MTU across AZs, and confirm ICMP delivery with provider.

grace (sre): ack taking oncall. I'll create a follow-up runbook ticket with action items: audit-jumbo-hosts-us-east-2, persistent-mss-policy, provider-icm-verify. Also will draft customer postmortem template.

customer-ops: Noted. We're sending targeted comms to impacted customers now.

devon (eng-oncall): one more datapoint: DNS resolvers in AZ2 were returning AAAA records faster than A for some endpoints -> some clients prefer v6 and get into the broken path. As part of the long-term fix we should consider v6 preference fallback logic in the client libs.

sam (neteng): agreed. we'll add an intermediate NAT64/464XLAT testbed for validating dual-stack behavior under MTU variance.

grace (sre): closing timeline: incident created 1782345678, MSS clamp applied 1782345824, provider confirmed ACL planned removal 1782345900 (expected). Will keep incident channel updated. I'm creating the postmortem draft and assigning owners.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity downgraded to P2; monitoring.

devon (eng-oncall): thanks team. I'll stay reachable if anything regresses.

pat (infra): rolling audit to find all hosts with nonstandard MTU scheduled for today. script: ```for h in $(list-hosts --az us-east-2); do ssh $h 'ip link show | grep mtu' ; done```

grace (sre): handoff complete. end of thread."
